result.text: A guest enters the restaurant when feeling hungry.
He chooses a dish from the changing meal range and waits until it is his turn.
Following this he places his order with the employee.
The employee enters the order into the POS system and collects the money from the guest.
After the payment, the employee sets up a buzzer and passes it on to the guest with the following information: "When the buzzer rings, your dinner is ready".
Afterwards the employee informs the chef of the new meal order.
The chef prepares the meal and places it in the service hatch.
He then informs the employee that he has placed the finished meal in the service hatch.
As soon as the employee is aware that the meal is ready he sets off the guest's buzzer.
This is how the guest finds out that his meal is ready for collection.
He can pick up his meal and eat it.
As soon as the guest appears at the service hatch, the employee hands over his meal.
Should a guest not react to the buzzer, the employee calls for him after 5 minutes, if necessary several times in a row.

result.rule: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

result.rule: When the description places ongoing activities within a stated period and separately says that the period ends before subsequent work, without explicitly requiring those activities to finish first: Model the period-ending trigger as a timer catch event leading to the subsequent work; do not add a parallel join that waits for every ongoing activity to complete unless the description requires that synchronization.

When the description states a conditional path but does not specify what happens when the condition is false: If an end event is modeled for that unspecified path, label it neutrally rather than assigning an unstated outcome.

When the description states a distinct handling action to be performed after an item or material is received: Model that handling action as a BPMN activity in the described flow; do not omit it or absorb it into another activity.

When the description states a milestone followed by later activities or ongoing support before the process is complete: Label the end event with the actual process-ending outcome, not with an earlier milestone; keep that milestone on its corresponding activity.

result.rule: Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.

result.rule: When the description states that one participant sends information, a request, or an item to another participant.: Model the stated exchange as a message flow from the sending participant to the receiving participant, connecting appropriate interaction nodes in their respective pools and directing the flow from sender to receiver.

When the description states an action from the perspective of the person or participant receiving a service, item, or information: Label the BPMN activity to preserve the direction and perspective stated in the description; do not recast it as the corresponding sender-side action.

When the description focuses on one participant’s workflow and mentions an outside party only as the recipient or source of requests, payments, or responses, without describing that party’s own process: Model the described workflow within its participant pool; do not add a separate pool or message flows solely to represent those mentions. Represent relevant receipt or decision points within the described process.
